name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It preserves fine details in complex scenes better than generic upscalers, giving a measurable boost to output quality without extra compute cost. The trade-off is extra setup time to integrate the ComfyUI node, but the model’s open-source status means no licensing fees or hidden limits.

name: Torque
text: InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop—it only sharpens geometry, not identity. The real risk is wasted effort: integrating ComfyUI adds pipeline complexity for a 0.5% bump that won’t move the needle on the actual failure mode. Test RealVisXL’s face model first—if it recovers lost detail, that’s a 2% gain with zero new tools; if not, we pivot to a face-specific super-resolution model like GFPGAN 2.0.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face model locks us into another proprietary black box—its "latest" claim is unverified, and Anthropic’s own 404s prove model access isn’t guaranteed. Instead, test InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler *only* on face crops first; if it fails, we pivot to open-source alternatives like FLUX’s face enhancer. The tiebreaker: run both on 100 identical face frames—whichever wins by >0.5% PSNR settles it.
